issue: The figure title says 'canonical 70B FP16', but the QLoRA bar is explicitly 4-bit NF4, not FP16. The title therefore mislabels the precision of one of the three scenarios.
evidence: Title: 'Memory floor: inference vs fine-tuning (canonical 70B FP16)'. Figure note: 'QLoRA: 4-bit (NF4) base + LoRA adapters + a small optimizer.' Caption: 'QLoRA fits ~50–70 GB on a single GPU.'
acceptance_test: Retitle to 'canonical 70B model (FP16 unless noted)' or '70B memory floor across precision/state scenarios'; verify the title no longer implies all three bars are FP16.

issue: The figure and caption label the 989 TFLOPS plateau as 'dense (no sparsity) FP16', but 989 TFLOPS is the sparse FP16 datasheet peak; dense FP16 is ~494.5 TFLOPS. The ridge points (295 and 206) are therefore computed from a sparse peak while claiming dense.
evidence: Caption: 'dense (no sparsity) FP16; the ceilings are peak/theoretical datasheet values'. Chart: 'compute plateau = 989 TFLOPS', 'ridge ≈ 295', 'ridge ≈ 206'. NVIDIA H100 datasheet: 989 TFLOPS FP16 with sparsity, 494.5 TFLOPS dense.
acceptance_test: Either relabel as sparse FP16 and remove 'dense (no sparsity)' from the caption, or replot with 494.5 TFLOPS dense: H100 ridge ≈ 148 FLOP/byte, H200 ridge ≈ 103 FLOP/byte; update all dependent text and the prefill/decode classification if needed.

issue: Several annotations are set in small, low-contrast orange/green text (e.g., 'memory-bound slope (≈ intensity × BW)', 'prefill 9.2K (intensity ≈ 9.2K FLOP/byte)', 'compute plateau = 989 TFLOPS') and may be difficult to read at print size.
evidence: Rendered page 157: these labels are visibly smaller than the axis labels and use light orange/green on white; no halo or outline.
acceptance_test: Increase font size to at least 8 pt and use darker colors or a white halo; verify legibility at 100% print size.
